method: built-in image edit of original guide plus identity only

attempts.prompt: EDIT IMAGE1, a grey pose mannequin, into a finished painted game sprite of the man in IMAGE2. Return exactly 1024 x 1536 pixels, real transparent RGBA. Keep everything IMAGE1 says about the pose and the camera: the size of the figure, where the head, trunk, arms, legs and boots are, the lean, the 45 degree turn and the 2:1 isometric camera 30 degrees down. The legs are the grey legs: paint each trouser thigh, knee, shin and boot over the grey one, in the same place and at the same angles; do not re-pose, straighten, mirror, recentre, enlarge or shrink anything. He walks toward the upper right of the picture; we see his back and his right side in three quarters, never a face from the front. Pose 1 of 4, contact: his right leg, on the picture's right, leads with the heel down and the toe up; his left leg trails on the picture's left, toe down and heel lifted; left arm forward, right arm back. IMAGE2 shows only his upper body, cut off at the hips and at half the size: take from it his head, hair, beard, moss-green flat cap, rust-orange and forest-green checked flannel shirt with rolled sleeves, skin and build, as a painting at the guide's size. Paint his legs yourself: charcoal-grey work trousers with turned-up cuffs, dark brown leather boots. The grey bar on his right shoulder in IMAGE1 is his axe: paint it as his wood-handled felling axe resting on his right shoulder, held by his right hand where the guide's hand is, the head behind his shoulder; his left arm swings as the guide's does. No other tool. Style: painted, broad smooth clusters of three or four shades per material, one light from the upper left, dark only on the lower and side rims, no outline round the whole figure, muted natural colours; nothing at or above cursor white #ECE4D0 and nothing as strong as selection amber #E8AA48. Alpha 0 background and an opaque figure; no ground, floor, shadow, glow, haze, text, border or extra object.

5.status: Requires visual isolation of shoulder tops when axe or cap intersects the columns

visualReview.reason: The axe head obscures the picture-left shoulder-to-neck junction and the shaft crosses the right shoulder; both shoulder tops cannot be isolated confidently.
visualReview.verdict: Back of head and right side visible, no front face; turned as guide by eye.
